issue_context.title: FileStorage does not handle properly an empty yml file
issue_context.body:
Under OpenCV 4.2.*, using cv::FileStorage to open an (invalid) empty yml file (0 bytes) results in resource leaking by not closing files properly.
With current 4.3.0 dev, there is even a crash by nullptr dereference when trying to check the BOM.

---

relates #16488

review_comments:
> closeFile();

Lets try to handle that in caller code instead (in single place).

I am afraid of regressions by trying to refactor error handling too much.
-the current FileStorage::~FileStorage destructor does not call closeFile(), and I don't know why
-the current FileStorage::open() has some try{...}catch(...){is_opened = true;release();throw;} (line 774) that rethrow an exception, but still marks the files as open, so there should not be a parent try{}catch{} pattern that would close files on exception.

perhaps a robust solution to avoid resource leaking could be to use local FILE* variables in the FileStorage::open(), with some RAII pattern (std::unique_ptr with custom deleter), and moving this local FILE* to this->file/this->gzFile only on success. With such a pattern, calling closeFile() on error won't be required.
the unique_ptr<> won't be a practical solution, because open() needs to call puts() and rewind() that require file and gzfile members to be initialized
